claim: On average, state-of-the-art NAS algorithms perform similarly to random architecture selection when evaluated with a fair, matched-conditions framework isolating the search phase from downstream task results.
stance_target: the strength/validity of random-search baselines as a bar for NAS methods to clear, a methodology standard the target paper's random-search comparison must be held to
scope_conditions: standard CNN search space used for weight sharing and NAS-Bench-101, ICLR 2020
quoted_support: On average, the state-of-the-art NAS algorithms perform similarly to the random policy

claim: The widely-used weight sharing strategy degrades the ranking of NAS candidates to the point of not reflecting their true performance, reducing the effectiveness of the search process -- a methodological confound reviewers should check for.
stance_target: methodological rigor standards for NAS evaluation, specifically confounds from weight-sharing/one-shot evaluation
scope_conditions: one-shot/weight-sharing NAS methods (e.g. DARTS, ENAS style)
quoted_support: the widely-used weight sharing strategy degrades the ranking of the NAS candidates to the point of not reflecting their true performance, thus reducing the effectiveness of the search process.
